sentences.text: This is the first application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.448/2023 registered at Police Station Audyogik Nagar Kshetra, District Ratlam (M.P.) for the offence under Sections 376(2)(N) and 323 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860.
The applicant is in custody since 06/07/2023.
2. As per prosecution story, prosecutrix and applicant both were having love affairs and were living in live-in relationship for last two and half years.
On 05/07/2023 prosecutrix made a complaint before the police station by stating that she know the applicant for last four years.

On 12/06/2023,
in the night prosecutrix and applicant were talking in a room, when the accused saw some photographs in the mobile of the prosecutrix and assaulted her from where she ran away.

Applicant committed rape upon her and also threatened her that if she will not continue relationship with him,

sentences.text: he will viral the photographs.
Accordingly, offence has been registered against the applicant.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant is an innocent person and he has been falsely implicated in this offence.
He is in custody since 06/07/2023.
Investigation is over and charge sheet has been filed.
Prosecutrix herself stated that she was having monetary terms with the applicant.
Prosecutrix is 20 years old major lady and applicant is also a young person of 20 years of age.
Applicant is permanent resident of Ratlam district.
Final conclusion of the trial is likely to take sufficient long time.
Under the above circumstances, prayer for grant of bail may be considered on such terms and conditions, as this Court deems fit and proper.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent / State opposes the bail application and prays for its rejection by submitting that prosecutrix has supported the case of prosecution in her statement under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C.
Hence, he is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.

5. Learned counsel for the objector / mother of the prosecutrix also opposes the bail application by submitting that applicant's family members are regularly threatening and pressuring the prosecutrix and her family members for compromise.
If the applicant is enlarged on bail, he may be a danger for the prosecutrix and her family members.
6. Perused the impugned order of the trial Court as well as the case diary.

7. After considering all the facts and circumstances of the case, nature and gravity of offence,
arguments advanced by the learned counsel for the applicant and also taking note of the fact that prosecutrix is a major lady and is doing some private job; from perusal of her statement under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. it appears that prosecutrix was living in the company of applicant for a period of about 04 years; FIR has been lodged after a lapse of about two years; after consuming phenyl the statement of prosecutrix has been recorded, in which she has not stated anything against the present applicant regarding the aforesaid offence; investigation is over, therefore, no further custodial interrogation of the applicant is required and final conclusion of the trial will take sufficient long time.
In these circumstances, I deem it proper to release the applicant on bail.
Therefore, without commenting on the merits of the case, the application is allowed.

8. It is directed that applicant be released on bail on his furnishing personal bond in the sum of Rs.75,000/- (Rupees Seventy Five Thousand Only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court for his appearance before the trial Court, as and when required.

He shall abide by all the conditions enumerated under Section 437(3) Cr.P.C.
Certified copy as per rules.
(ANIL VERMA) JUDGE Tej Chitransh @ Honey vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh
